title: Particle Model and States of Matter (KS3 Chemistry)
subject: Chemistry
strapline: How particles are arranged in solids, liquids and gases.
facts: All matter is made of tiny particles that are always moving.
In a solid, particles are packed closely in a regular pattern and only vibrate — solids keep their shape.
In a liquid, particles are close but can move past each other — liquids flow and take the container’s shape.
In a gas, particles are far apart and move quickly in all directions — gases fill their container.
Heating gives particles more energy so they move more and can change state.
Changes of state: melting, freezing, evaporating/boiling, condensing and (solid↔gas) subliming.
Changes of state are physical changes — no new substance is made and they can be reversed.

quick_quiz.q: In which state are particles far apart and fast-moving?
What is the change from liquid to gas called?
Is a change of state a physical or chemical change?

teacher_tips: Use particle diagrams and role-play "be the particles" to embed arrangement.
Stress that particles themselves don’t change size when heated — spacing does.
Separate physical (state) change from chemical change explicitly.
